title: Split over-cap scheduler sources graph-internal.ts and frontier.ts
description: Objective: bring packages/scheduler/src/graph-internal.ts (415 physical lines) and packages/scheduler/src/frontier.ts (412) under the per-file cap - target <=250, hard split bar 400 (AGENTS.md source rails; epic rails: the cap is per FILE). MEASURED at HEAD 7183c04 via wc -l on 2026-08-09. Scope: mechanical decomposition into focused modules preserving the existing public surface of @moe/scheduler exactly (root exports unchanged, behavior identical); update intra-package imports; keep .js runtime bridges consistent with the package existing pattern. NOT in scope: behavior changes, new exports, touching other packages. Note: generated packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts (896 lines) is deliberately excluded as generated code; if a cap exemption for generated files is wanted, that is a governor decision, not this task. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/src/** only. Verification: pnpm typecheck && pnpm test.

implementationPlan.description: Ground the refactor before editing. Record the current task-base SHA, `git status --porcelain -- packages/scheduler/src`, exact physical line counts for graph-internal.ts/frontier.ts using a CRLF/LF-aware byte splitter, SHA-256 hashes of both sources, the exact 36-name root namespace from index-surface.test.ts, and the byte contents of graph-internal.js/frontier.js. Run the task's pre-diff baseline once and retain every failing path for the path-attributed comparison; the planning baseline already observed scheduler typecheck green and only foreign `apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts` red through package-boundary.test.ts. Inventory all imports of graph-internal.js/frontier.js and freeze the rule that no consumer, package index, or test file will be edited. Treat the existing scheduler tests as held-out characterization coverage because there is no behavior change.

Mechanically extract traversal algorithms from packages/scheduler/src/graph-internal.ts into new graph-traversal.ts plus its exact one-line LF `.js` bridge. Move `compareStrings`, the private traversal-counter bump helper, `TopoResult`, `IndexMinHeap`, `topologicalOrder`, `CycleCore`, and `findCycleCore` without changing branches, counter increments, sort keys, issue facts, or return shapes. graph-traversal.ts may import `HardGraphIndex` only as an erased type and `TraversalCounter` from graph-model; it must not runtime-import graph-internal. In graph-internal.ts, import the moved comparator/counter used by buildHardGraphIndex and explicitly re-export the same previously available moved values/types so all existing intra-package imports remain byte-compatible. Keep GraphStructureView, bit, sortedCopy, makeIssue, sortIssues, deepFreeze, HardArc/HardGraphIndex/buildHardGraphIndex, edgeKeysOf, framing, and computeGraphIdentity in graph-internal. Do not export the new helper from packages/scheduler/src/index.ts.

Mechanically extract the hostile cursor front half of partitionFrontier into new frontier-cursor.ts plus its exact one-line LF `.js` bridge. The helper owns CURSOR_KEYS/HARD_EDGE_FACT_KEYS, satisfaction validation, exact own-data-property cursor reads, safe array-length reads, absolute ceilings before any indexed read, dense-array shape validation, HARD-edge fact shape/unknown/duplicate/missing checks, and the resulting edge-state map. Return a discriminated internal result that distinguishes fatal schema/count/density issues (frontier.ts must immediately route them through its existing `fail`) from accumulated HARD-edge issues plus the safely admitted node-fact array/count (frontier.ts must continue node parsing so combined issue ordering is unchanged). Keep runtime provenance first, NODE_FACT_KEYS and node fact parsing, issue aggregation, readiness partitioning/counter updates, canonical sort/freeze, and `registerFrontierPartition` in frontier.ts. The helper must not freeze/sort final outcomes, register provenance, infer node readiness, or be exported from the package root.

Finish the internal composition without widening scope: remove now-unused imports/constants from the two keeper files, retain explanatory hostile-read and zero-authority comments at their owning boundary, and ensure all six production files are focused and <=250 physical lines (split before 400; do not compress logic into unreadable one-liners merely to hit the target). Keep packages/scheduler/src/index.ts, every `*.test.ts`, graph-internal.js, and frontier.js unchanged. Confirm by inspection that existing consumers still import graph-internal.js/frontier.js, the two new helper specifiers appear only in their keeper modules, the helpers never import the keepers at runtime, and no new package-root symbol is introduced.

Adversarial self-review the completed diff as a behavior-preserving move. Compare moved graph declarations against the recorded pre-split blob and prove their bodies are byte-contained apart from necessary export/import relocation, absent from graph-internal.ts after the move, and not duplicated. Prove index.ts and all scheduler tests are unchanged, both new bridges are exact LF one-liners, all six production files are <=250 physical lines with a CRLF/LF-aware Node/Python counter, and the import graph has no runtime cycle or root export. Then mutation-drill the held-out production surface: after copying each new/uncommitted helper to an OS-temp backup and recording SHA-256, (a) change the topological acyclic guard or one traversal counter increment in graph-traversal.ts and require an unchanged scheduler suite to go red, and (b) change `FRONTIER_EDGE_FACT_MISSING` or bypass a cursor ceiling in frontier-cursor.ts and require the exact refusal/hostile-input test to go red. Restore from the external backups, verify hashes exactly, delete temp files, and leave no mutation/probe artifact. Review duplicate execution, null/proxy/accessor/huge cursor inputs, issue precedence, UNKNOWN handling, determinism, freezing, counter complexity, and foreign shared-tree changes before proceeding.

Run the single final verification command exactly: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`. Record fresh foreground output and exit status. Compare repo-wide failing paths at HEAD with the pre-diff baseline and apply the path-attributed rule: do not claim success if this diff adds any scheduler-owned failure; report any residual foreign failure verbatim with exact file/test lines. Confirm the exact 36-name @moe/scheduler root surface test passes, scheduler suites covering topology, determinism, complexity, immutability, hostile cursor input, frontier reason codes, and runtime bridges are green, and every resulting production file remains <=250 physical lines. Before completion, inspect `git status --porcelain`; unstage any foreign path without touching its bytes, then commit only `packages/scheduler/src/graph-internal.ts packages/scheduler/src/graph-traversal.ts packages/scheduler/src/graph-traversal.js packages/scheduler/src/frontier.ts packages/scheduler/src/frontier-cursor.ts packages/scheduler/src/frontier-cursor.js` by explicit pathspec and verify `git show --stat` contains only those paths.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: two focused internal extractions while retaining the existing files as the only import facades. `graph-traversal.ts` receives comparator/counter support plus heap-based topological order and Tarjan SCC cycle-core detection; `graph-internal.ts` explicitly imports/re-exports those established internal names, so every current consumer stays unchanged. `frontier-cursor.ts` receives hostile-safe cursor framing, ceiling/dense-shape checks, and HARD-edge fact parsing; `frontier.ts` keeps provenance admission, node-fact parsing, readiness partitioning, final canonical sort/freeze, and `registerFrontierPartition`. Rejected: changing every consumer to import the new graph helper directly (unnecessary churn and a wider review surface); a four-or-more-module split (not required to meet the per-file cap); duplicating validators/comparators; changing public exports or tests. TDD test creation and docs updates are consciously skipped because this is a behavior-neutral decomposition: the existing unchanged scheduler suites and exact root-surface test are held-out oracles, then mutation-drilled after the move.

Existing graph-internal.js and frontier.js are exact one-line `.ts` bridges. packages/scheduler/src/index.ts publishes partitionFrontier only and index-surface.test.ts pins the exact 36-value @moe/scheduler namespace; neither file needs modification. Measured graph seam: keep GraphStructureView/bit/sortedCopy/issues/freezing/buildHardGraphIndex/edgeKeysOf/identity in graph-internal; move compareStrings, the private traversal-counter bump, TopoResult, IndexMinHeap, topologicalOrder, CycleCore and findCycleCore together. graph-traversal may import HardGraphIndex type-only, avoiding a runtime cycle; graph-internal imports the moved comparator/counter and explicitly re-exports the existing moved names. Measured frontier order: runtime provenance -> exact cursor schema -> safe lengths -> raw ceilings before indexed reads -> dense shape -> HARD-edge facts/missing facts -> node facts/missing facts -> fail once on accumulated issues -> partition -> freeze/register. The helper must return fatal issues separately from accumulated HARD-edge issues so frontier.ts preserves this exact order and remains the only final sort/freeze/provenance owner. Fresh narrow baseline: @moe/scheduler typecheck exited 0; scheduler test had 35 files pass/1 fail and 674 tests pass/1 fail solely because package-boundary.test.ts scanned foreign apps/daemon/src/daemon-main.ts and found an unterminated regular-expression token. That failing path is outside this task and must be recorded in the worker's pre-diff baseline, not hidden.
planningNotes.risks: Do not introduce a graph-internal <-> graph-traversal runtime cycle: the helper's HardGraphIndex reference must be `import type`, while graph-internal owns the only runtime import direction. Preserve the comparator and counter increments byte-for-byte; traversal-count complexity tests will expose drift. Frontier extraction is especially order-sensitive: ceiling checks must precede every element/property read, hostile accessors/proxies must still deny without invocation, HARD and node issues must still accumulate before the one canonical sort, and UNKNOWN must not become satisfied. The helper must not deep-freeze, sort final issues, register provenance, or become a package-root export. New bridges must be exactly one LF-terminated export line. Existing tests and index.ts are held out and must not be edited. Shared-tree foreign red from daemon-main.ts is an attributed baseline only; never repair or revert it. During mutation drills, back up new/uncommitted helper bytes outside the repository and verify SHA-256 restoration because a foreign completion hook can sweep live mutations into a commit.
